rationale: All three lenses ran against the full branch diff with the approved spec, so confidence is high. Six blocking findings: two critical and four major. Critical 1: PR #575's stricter isMultiProviderConfig makes a previously accepted global config look empty, so the next global save overwrites every global profile. Critical 2: local-config migrations still bypass the B1 safe-write path. Major: inquirer Ctrl+C reported as a failure, AC10 test gaps, an inaccurate guide line, and the @/ alias constraint. 7 deferred as pre-existing on main: read path silently ignores unparseable/BOM local files; Object.prototype and __proto__ profile names; no file locking or atomic writes; cwd == home makes local and global the same file; empty global activeProfile loads built-in defaults; rename to an empty name; global save then local repair is not atomic. 16 dismissed: false positives (typecheck/lint pass, test path isolation via ConfigLoader getters), decisions the approved spec/plan made (first remaining profile on delete, activation on update, label wording, shared workspace, uniqueness is a non-goal), and below-floor edge cases.

findings.title: Guide claims system-wide unique profile names
findings.problem: The Key rule still says 'Profile names are unique across the system'. Nothing enforces cross-scope uniqueness on add (non-goal, PR #585); only rename and setup check the current directory's scopes.
findings.impact: Readers and agents rely on a guarantee the code does not give, e.g. assume delete/rename cannot hit a same-named profile in the other scope.
findings.recommendation: Reword to the actual rule: rename and setup reject a name that already exists in this directory's local or global scope; duplicates across scopes resolve local first.

findings.title: AC10 command-level regression gaps
findings.problem: No command-level test asserts the AC1 'deleted from global config' output. AC8 red-reason output is tested only for delete and rename, not for status or the auth commands.
findings.impact: Regressions in the user-visible scope message or in a catch block reverting to silent logger.error would not be caught.
findings.recommendation: Add command tests: delete success prints the owning scope; status failure and login/logout/refresh failure print the red reason and exit 1.

findings.title: New file uses deep relative imports
findings.problem: command-error.ts imports '../../../utils/logger.js' and '../../../utils/errors.js'; the approved spec/plan constraints require @/ aliases for new cross-tree imports.
findings.impact: Violates a documented project constraint (AGENTS.md pitfalls).

findings.title: Inquirer Ctrl+C shown as a red failure
findings.problem: Ctrl+C in an inquirer prompt (delete confirmation, setup prompts) throws inquirer's ExitPromptError, not ProfileSelectionCancelledError. exitWithCommandError prints '✗ Failed to delete profile: User force closed the prompt...' and exits 1.
findings.impact: A user cancel looks like a failure. This output is new on this branch (before, the exit was silent), and it contradicts B6's clean-cancellation intent.
findings.recommendation: Treat error.name === 'ExitPromptError' like ProfileSelectionCancelledError (yellow 'Cancelled.', exit 0) and add a test.

findings.title: Stricter guard lets global saves wipe profiles
findings.problem: PR #575 made isMultiProviderConfig reject a v2 global config with a null/array profile entry or a non-string activeProfile. Main accepted such files. loadMultiProviderConfig now treats them as empty ({version:2, activeProfile:'default', profiles:{}}), and saveMultiProviderConfig (saveProfile, saveUserEmail, switch, delete, rename) then writes that over the real file.
findings.impact: Data loss: one hand-edited bad entry turns the next global save into a wipe of every global profile. This is a regression on this branch.
findings.recommendation: Mirror B1 for the global write path: before saveMultiProviderConfig writes, re-read the raw global file and refuse with a ConfigurationError naming the file ('left unchanged') when it exists and is not missing/empty, v2 or legacy. Add a test that a global file with a null profile entry is byte-identical after saveProfile/switchProfile.

findings.title: Migrations bypass the B1 safe local write
findings.problem: Migrations 004, 005 and 007 load the local file with loadLocalMultiProviderConfig. Through loadJsonConfig it returns {} for unparseable JSON or a BOM-prefixed file, which becomes an empty v2 config. The migrations then save it with saveLocalMultiProviderConfig.
findings.impact: A pending migration can replace an existing local file wholesale (profiles, assistants and workspace lost). This violates the B1 caller list and the anti-goal.
findings.recommendation: Make loadLocalMultiProviderConfig read through readLocalConfigForWrite (BOM strip, refuse unparseable/legacy/unsupported with ConfigurationError, fill partial files) so migrations refuse instead of overwriting. Keep the missing-file default. Add a test that a migration on an unparseable local file leaves it byte-identical.
